title: Pure-tensor description and coherence of the pro-etale inverse-image tensor comparison
statement:
Let $h:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image $h^{-1}$ on sheaves of sets, rings and modules, with adjunction unit $\eta_h:\mathcal H\to h_*h^{-1}\mathcal H$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For an object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $s\in\mathcal H(V)$ write $h^{-1}s\in(h^{-1}\mathcal H)(T'\times_TV)$ for the image of $s$ under $\eta_h$. Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so that $h^{-1}\mathcal F,h^{-1}\mathcal G$ are sheaves of $h^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules. Use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and for $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $t\in\mathcal G(V)$ write $s\otimes t$ also for the image in $(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)(V)$ of the presheaf pure tensor.

1. There is a unique morphism of sheaves of $h^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules
$$\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:h^{-1}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)\longrightarrow h^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O}h^{-1}\mathcal G$$
such that $\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}(h^{-1}(s\otimes t))=h^{-1}s\otimes h^{-1}t$ over $T'\times_TV$ for every object $V$ and all $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $t\in\mathcal G(V)$. It is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.

2. Let $\phi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be $\mathcal O'$-modules, regarded also as $\mathcal O$-modules through $\phi$ (and $h^{-1}\mathcal F,h^{-1}\mathcal G$ as $h^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules through $h^{-1}\phi$). Let $\pi:\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O'}\mathcal G$ and $\pi':h^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O}h^{-1}\mathcal G\to h^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O'}h^{-1}\mathcal G$ be the maps sending $s\otimes t$ to $s\otimes t$. Then $\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}\circ h^{-1}(\pi)=\pi'\circ\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}$, the left $\sigma^h$ taken over $\mathcal O'$ and the right one over $\mathcal O$.

3. Let $g:T''\to T'$ be a second morphism of schemes. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\gamma:(h\circ g)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}h^{-1}$ of functors on sheaves of sets with $\gamma\bigl((h\circ g)^{-1}s\bigr)=g^{-1}(h^{-1}s)$ over $T''\times_TV\cong T''\times_{T'}(T'\times_TV)$ for all $V$ and $s\in\mathcal H(V)$; it is the composition isomorphism of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] (5), and it carries the ring and module structures of $(h\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal O$, $(h\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal F$ to those of $g^{-1}h^{-1}\mathcal O$, $g^{-1}h^{-1}\mathcal F$. With the target tensor identified along $\gamma_{\mathcal O}$,
$$\sigma^g_{h^{-1}\mathcal F,h^{-1}\mathcal G}\circ g^{-1}\bigl(\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}\bigr)\circ\gamma_{\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G}=(\gamma_{\mathcal F}\otimes\gamma_{\mathcal G})\circ\sigma^{h\circ g}_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}.$$
For $h=\mathrm{id}_T$ the unit $\eta_{\mathrm{id}}$ is an isomorphism, and under it $\sigma^{\mathrm{id}}_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}$ is the identity of $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G$.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient quotient by the sectionwise balanced tensor pairing and the module sheafification adjunction. Uniqueness follows by adjunction injectivity and tensor induction. Construct comparison_exists by pairing the two canonical module units into the tensor of their targets, using the general private tensorPushforwardPairing_exists for independent site universes, then transpose through the canonical module adjunction. Its unit formula is the prescribed inverseSection, and the same tensor universal property gives uniqueness.

Obtain ringSetsIdentification by the forgetful pullback comparison. For moduleSetsIdentification, use the isomorphism of the abelian unit mate for the canonical module adjunction, followed by the forgetful pullback comparison. Both identifications have the required set-unit normalization, and adjunction injectivity gives their uniqueness.

For scalarIdentification, regard the S-module unit as R-linear using naturality of the ring unit with the scalar map, and transpose it. For moduleId, restrict along pullbackId; the conjugation unit equation proves compatibility with the identity ring comparison. For moduleComp, compose the two module units and apply sectionwise restriction along the fibre-product associator. The ring compositor unit equation proves this section map linear, and naturality of the units and associator proves it natural; then transpose. In all three cases the normalized underlying-set maps identify the underlying map with an isomorphism, so reflection of isomorphisms proves invertibility. The module adjunction proves uniqueness.

The conjugation unit equation for the existing set compositor, naturality of the two maps of underlying sets, and naturality of the second set unit give setComp_map_units. This proves the underlying-set normalization used for moduleComp. Injectivity of the composite set adjunction gives setComp_unique and the ring and module compositor equations. The identity set pullback is equivalent to the identity functor by conjugating lowerStarId, so its adjunction unit is invertible.

Build a private algebraic inverse-image lift whose module functor is definitionally the recorded inverse image. Its natural underlying-set identification is the normalized moduleSetsIdentification. Transpose naturality and each operation-graph equation through the set adjunction. Ring-unit preservation of operations and module-unit preservation of addition and scalar multiplication prove the equations, giving an explicit lift with no data chosen from mere existence.

Apply the independent-universe normalized tensor construction with scalar map identity and the explicitly defined functor F followed by sheafified extension of scalars along identity. Sectionwise extendScalarsId and the sheafification counit give the identity scalar-extension isomorphism, normalized on 1 tensor m. Identify the localized monoidal tensor with the explicit site tensor by the identity isomorphism of their presheaf tensors and sheafification. Conjugate the general tensor isomorphism by these isomorphisms. Evaluate its generalized pure-tensor formula on the set-unit image of (m,n) in the cartesian product of underlying module sheaves. Naturality of the unit with each projection and the pure pairing gives exactly comparison_exists normalization; uniqueness identifies its map with comparison and proves invertibility.

Maps out of F(M tensor N) are equal if they agree on all inverse images of original pure tensors: transpose through the canonical module adjunction, then use tensor sheafification and tensor induction. Apply this criterion to joint naturality, coefficient change, tensor composition and identity. Naturality of module units, the quotient normalization, moduleComp normalization and moduleId normalization turn both sides of each square into the same pure tensor. This proves every coherence clause without a local-generation assertion about original pulled-back sections.
